questions.question_text:
A rectangular prism has a base measuring $6\text{ cm}$ by $8\text{ cm}$ and a height of $9\text{ cm}$.
Find the length of its space diagonal.
Round to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Added the three edge lengths $6+8+9$ instead of adding their squares and taking the square root.
Stopped at the base face diagonal $\sqrt{6^{2}+8^{2}}$ and left out the height.
Used only the base edge of $8\text{ cm}$ and the height, calculating $\sqrt{8^{2}+9^{2}}$, and left out the other base edge.
Treated the space diagonal as a face diagonal, giving $a^{2}=12^{2}/2=72$ and surface area $6\times72=432\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Divided the diagonal by $3$ to get an edge of $4\text{ cm}$, then calculated $6\times4^{2}=96\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Halved the diagonal to get an edge of $6\text{ cm}$, then calculated $6\times6^{2}=216\text{ cm}^{2}$.

questions.solution_text:
For edge length $a$, $\sqrt{3a^{2}}=12$.
$3a^{2}=144$
$a^{2}=48$
Surface area: $6a^{2}=6\times48=288\text{ cm}^{2}$
